evidence: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp only calls FulfilmentService methods (listProducts, getProduct, addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, transition, cancelOrder); it never uses the repositories directly

src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: GET /orders reuses the domain's isOrderState instead of re-implementing the state check; DomainError kinds map to HTTP codes in one place, the STATUS const plus the error middleware

src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository, with only storage and query logic (get/list/save/nextId)
src/infrastructure/server.ts: composition root that builds FulfilmentService with the in-memory repositories and seeds data through service.addProduct, not through the repositories directly

Minor: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts builds the product response shape { id: p.id, name: p.name, stock: p.stock } inline in GET /products, GET /products/:id and POST /products. This is repeated presentation code, not a duplicated invariant
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/infrastructure module is one coherent adapter layer. It holds an HTTP adapter (http-app.ts), in-memory persistence adapters that implement the application ports (in-memory-repositories.ts), and a composition root (server.ts). Each file uses the module's own abstractions consistently:
- http-app.ts goes only through FulfilmentService. It never touches repositories directly.
- server.ts wires the repositories into the service and seeds data through service.addProduct. It does not write to the repositories directly.
- The repositories only store and query data. They hold no domain rules.
The HTTP layer checks request shape (types of id, name, stock, customerId, items). That is transport-level validation, not a copy of a domain invariant. The order-state check reuses the domain's isOrderState rather than re-implementing it, and error-to-status mapping lives in one place (STATUS plus the error middleware). One small issue: http-app.ts builds the product response shape { id, name, stock } inline three times instead of in one helper. That is repeated presentation code inside a single file, not a duplicated business rule or a bypassed abstraction, so it is not enough to fail the rubric.
